_comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for cljgo's defining forms.
Clojure has no declaration node type — `(defn f …)` is an ordinary list
whose HEAD symbol carries the meaning and whose SECOND element is the
name. Every consumer (editors + ctx-optimize) therefore needs the same
list of head symbols, and keeping four copies in sync by hand is how they
drift. Edit THIS file, then run:
which regenerates the tree-sitter query fragment, the VS Code TextMate
rule, the Emacs indent rules, and the ctx-optimize pack.
`kind` is the ctx-optimize node kind. `indent` is the Emacs/clojure-mode
indent spec. Adding your own project's definers is the supported path —
_not_definers: core.async's go / go-loop / thread / alt! / alt!! are CONTROL FLOW, not
defining forms — they bind nothing at the top level, so they belong in
highlights.scm (they are there) and NOT here. The macros themselves are
picked up normally, because core/async.cljg writes them as
Likewise `default` / `defaults` / `default-on` appear in head position in
this corpus but are ordinary fns whose names merely start with 'def'.
Matching is exact-text, so they are never mistaken for definers.
